bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is an AI subfield focused on systems learning from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns from data to make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial for modern tech, used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Recent growth due to large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised Learning, Unsupervised Learning, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: trains on labeled data to predict outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize rewards (e.g., robotics, gaming).
Model Training: feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust parameters.
Features and Labels: input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: data split for training the model and evaluating its performance.
Overfitting: model learns training data too well, performs poorly on new data.
Underfitting: model is too simple, fails to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: models linear relationship for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: used for classification, predicts probability of belonging to a class.
Decision Trees: non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): finds optimal hyperplane for classification, effective in high dimensions.
Neural Networks: inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment.
Finance: fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: evaluating model performance using separate datasets.
Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score for classification; MSE, R-squared for regression.
Cross-Validation: technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for best performance.
Data Quality and Quantity: need for large, accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: difficulty in understanding complex model decisions, especially in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: common issues affecting model generalization.
Continuous evolution with immense potential for applications.
Advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Growing role and integration into daily life across various industries.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential.
